name: Nasdaq, Inc.

profile.description: Nasdaq operates as a global technology company serving capital markets and other industries through three segments: Capital Access Platforms, Financial Technology, and Market Services. The company runs one of the world's largest stock exchanges, provides market data and index products, and offers financial crime detection (Verafin), regulatory reporting (AxiomSL), and cross-asset trading solutions (Calypso). Q2 2026 net revenue reached $1.5B (up 15% YoY) with diluted EPS of $1.07 (up 25% YoY) and ARR of $3.3B growing 12% organically [1].

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Nasdaq executed a transformative strategic pivot from a pure exchange operator to a diversified financial technology platform through the $10.5B Adenza acquisition in November 2023, adding AxiomSL (regulatory reporting) and Calypso (cross-asset trading) to create a comprehensive Financial Technology division alongside the organic build-out of Verafin's anti-financial crime platform [1][2]. This repositioned Nasdaq from a cyclical exchange business toward higher-margin, recurring technology revenue. AI Deployment (2/2): Verafin's Agentic AI Workforce platform is deployed across 650+ financial institutions for automated fraud detection and anti-money laundering, making it one of the most widely adopted AI products in financial services; the anti-financial crime business grew 20% YoY and continues accelerating, generating quantifiable AI-driven revenue [2]. Market Share (2/2): Nasdaq operates one of the world's largest stock exchanges, is the leading listing venue for technology IPOs, and its index business generated revenue growth of 38% in Q2 2026 driven by $750B+ in assets benchmarked to Nasdaq-branded indices; the Nasdaq-100 supports trillions in ETF assets [1]. Product Pipeline (1/2): AI-powered surveillance and compliance tools are expanding across AxiomSL and Calypso platforms, and Verafin continues adding agentic AI capabilities, but specific next-gen product launches with named dates and revenue visibility are limited beyond general AI and cloud expansion. R&D Intensity (1/1): Technology spending exceeds financial services industry averages, with Nasdaq investing heavily in cloud migration, AI infrastructure, and platform integration post-Adenza [2].

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): Nasdaq's purpose — championing inclusive growth and prosperity by powering stronger economies through efficient, transparent, and accessible capital markets — is specific, distinctive, and directly tied to strategic decisions including the Adenza acquisition to combat financial crime and the development of ESG reporting tools [2]. The mission connects financial infrastructure to economic democratization and has guided the transformation from exchange to technology platform. Community Impact (1/2): Nasdaq participates in UN Global Compact, UNPRI, and the Sustainable Stock Exchanges Initiative; the Nasdaq Entrepreneurial Center provides education and mentoring for entrepreneurs [3]. General corporate philanthropy and ESG leadership without specific dollar commitments. Employee Retention (1/2): CEO Adena Friedman has been with Nasdaq since 1993 (33 years), serving as CEO since 2017, demonstrating exceptional leadership tenure; CFO Sarah Youngwood and other senior leaders show multi-year tenures, but no specific voluntary turnover data or average employee tenure statistics are publicly available. Insider Buying (0/2): No evidence of meaningful net insider buying by Friedman or other executives in the last 12 months; insider activity appears dominated by compensation-plan dispositions and routine equity award sales.

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored as a Growth stock. Nasdaq demonstrates strong financial fundamentals: ROE of 16.5% exceeds the 15% target (score 1.0, 2x weight), and profit margin of 35.0% significantly exceeds the 20% target (score 1.0) [1]. Revenue growth of 14.9% YoY surpasses the 10% target (score 1.0), while estimated 5-year revenue CAGR of approximately 11% also exceeds the target (score 1.0, 2x weight), boosted by the Adenza acquisition and organic Solutions revenue growth [1]. D/E of 77.7% is slightly above the 70% target (score 0.97), reflecting acquisition-related debt that management is actively deleveraging. Forward P/E of 20.5 is near the 20 target (score 0.99). The PEG ratio of 1.52 sits between target and floor (score 0.74, 2x weight), reflecting moderate valuation premium relative to growth rate. Daily dollar volume of $296M provides ample liquidity.

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (7/9): Nasdaq's core exchange infrastructure is structurally protected from AI substitution — regulated securities exchanges, clearinghouses, and settlement systems require regulatory licenses, deep institutional trust, and network effects that AI cannot replicate or disintermediate [1][2]. The Financial Technology division (AxiomSL, Calypso, Verafin) provides mission-critical regulatory compliance and trading systems with high switching costs and regulatory embedding that create natural defensive moats. Index and data businesses benefit from proprietary brand moats and institutional data partnerships that gain value in an AI-driven world. However, some market data analytics and workflow products could face competitive pressure from AI-powered fintech alternatives offering faster and cheaper solutions. AI Opportunity (1/1): Verafin's Agentic AI Workforce platform generates direct AI revenue across 650+ financial institutions, and the anti-financial crime business grew 20% YoY with AI innovations making it Nasdaq's fastest-growing segment; AI-enhanced surveillance and compliance tools create additional AI-driven revenue streams across the platform [2].

infinite_game.summary: Nasdaq under Adena Friedman demonstrates infinite game thinking through a deliberate transformation from a cyclical exchange operator into a technology company powering global capital markets. The $10.5B Adenza acquisition — the largest in company history — sacrificed near-term earnings and tripled the debt load to build a durable, recurring-revenue platform that reduces dependence on volatile trading volumes. Friedman's 33-year tenure at Nasdaq and consistent strategic vision for technology-driven market infrastructure reflect a leader playing to keep playing rather than optimizing for quarterly results.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): Nasdaq's purpose — championing inclusive growth by powering stronger economies through efficient, transparent, and accessible capital markets — is genuinely distinctive and has been validated through the company's strategic transformation under Friedman from a pure exchange into a financial technology platform [2]. The cause connects market infrastructure to economic democratization, and strategic decisions (Adenza acquisition, Verafin build-out, ESG reporting tools) trace back to it. However, this refined purpose framing is relatively recent under Friedman and has not yet been tested through a leadership transition or major crisis that would prove durability.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Friedman's 33-year tenure at Nasdaq provides exceptional institutional continuity, and the leadership team includes several long-tenured executives including CFO Sarah Youngwood [2]. The shareholder letter emphasizes that attracting and retaining the best people is critical, and the company cultivates a culture of innovation and client centricity. However, no specific voluntary turnover data, employee satisfaction scores, or evidence of psychological safety distinguishes Nasdaq from financial services industry norms.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (1/1): Nasdaq competes with ICE/NYSE, CME Group, LSEG, and S&P Global but has differentiated through technology and AI rather than engaging in destructive price competition. Friedman has consistently framed competitors' strengths as motivation to invest in technology capabilities, and the Adenza acquisition was explicitly about building differentiated capabilities rather than simply growing exchange market share [2]. The company studies decentralized finance innovations from fintech rivals rather than dismissing them.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (2/2): Nasdaq has fundamentally reinvented itself from a single-market U.S. exchange into a global financial technology company, with the $10.5B Adenza acquisition representing the boldest strategic pivot in company history — accepting significant debt and near-term earnings dilution to build recurring technology revenue that now represents a growing majority of the business [1][2]. The Verafin acquisition (2021) earlier pivoted Nasdaq into anti-financial crime technology, creating an entirely new growth vector. Each transformation moved away from cyclical trading revenue toward durable technology revenue in service of the broader market infrastructure mission.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (2/2): Friedman demonstrated strategic courage by executing the $10.5B Adenza acquisition that significantly increased Nasdaq's debt load and diluted near-term earnings, betting that recurring financial technology revenue would create more durable long-term value than higher-margin but cyclical exchange revenue [1][2]. The company invested aggressively in AI through Verafin when financial crime technology was unproven at scale, and CFO Youngwood has articulated disciplined return-on-capital frameworks for AI investments rather than chasing hype, reflecting measured long-term thinking.

investment_thesis: Nasdaq at $96.12 with a $53.7B market cap has successfully transformed from a cyclical exchange operator into a high-margin financial technology platform, with Q2 2026 net revenue reaching $1.5B (up 15% YoY), diluted EPS of $1.07 (up 25%), and ARR of $3.3B growing 12% organically [1]. The Adenza integration is delivering with Solutions revenue growing 17% in Q2 and the Financial Technology segment contributing recurring, high-margin revenue that reduces dependence on volatile trading volumes. The AI-powered anti-financial crime business (Verafin) is the fastest-growing division, deployed across 650+ financial institutions with the Agentic AI Workforce platform, while index revenue surged 38% in Q2 driven by $750B+ in benchmarked assets [1][2]. Operating margins of 49.3% and free cash flow of $1.7B support rapid debt reduction while funding continued technology investment.
thesis_continued: The bear case centers on valuation and integration execution. At 20.5x forward earnings and a PEG of 1.52, Nasdaq trades at a premium to traditional exchange peers, pricing in continued double-digit growth that requires sustained Adenza cross-sell acceleration and AI-driven revenue expansion [1]. Debt-to-equity of 77.7% remains elevated from the $10.5B Adenza acquisition, and while deleveraging is on track, annual interest expense constrains capital flexibility. The board diversity rule controversy — though primarily a regulatory/legal issue — created reputational headwinds, and the SEC's evolving stance on exchange-imposed governance requirements adds regulatory uncertainty [3]. Market Services revenue remains tied to trading volumes that are inherently cyclical, and while this segment is a declining share of total revenue, a sustained downturn in capital markets activity would pressure overall growth. Competition from S&P Global, ICE/LSEG, and Bloomberg in financial data and technology is intensifying as multiple players target the same regulatory technology spending pool.
key_catalysts: Adenza integration delivering with Solutions revenue growing 17% in Q2 2026 and ARR reaching $3.3B; cross-selling AxiomSL and Calypso to Nasdaq's existing 6,000+ client base creates a large untapped revenue opportunity [1]

Verafin's Agentic AI Workforce platform expanding rapidly across 650+ financial institutions with 20%+ growth, positioning Nasdaq as the leading AI-powered anti-financial crime platform as regulatory enforcement intensifies globally [2]

Index revenue surging 38% in Q2 2026 driven by the secular passive investing trend and $750B+ in assets benchmarked to Nasdaq-branded indices, with new product launches expanding the addressable market [1]
key_risks: Elevated debt-to-equity of 77.7% from the $10.5B Adenza acquisition constrains financial flexibility; while deleveraging is progressing with strong free cash flow, interest expense reduces near-term earnings power [1]

Premium valuation at 20.5x forward earnings and PEG of 1.52 requires sustained double-digit organic growth execution; any integration stumbles or ARR growth deceleration could trigger multiple compression toward exchange-peer averages [1]

Market Services revenue remains exposed to cyclical trading volume fluctuations, and regulatory uncertainty around exchange-imposed governance requirements and SEC oversight creates ongoing headline risk [3]
